newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope urges hostage-takers to free captives.
newsitem.headline: Pope urges hostage-takers to free captives.

text.p: Pope John Paul, in an apparent appeal to Marxist guerrillas holding 74 hostages in Peru, on Sunday urged kidnappers and hostage-takers to free their captives as a "gesture of humanity".

"The mercy of Christ, born of human weakness, urges hostage-takers to fulfil this gesture of humanity -- free these people," the Pope said. His made no direct reference to the Peru crisis, now in its 19th day, but said his thoughts and prayers were with families missing loved ones over the Christmas period.

The Polish Pontiff, speaking to pilgrims in St Peter's Square at his regular Sunday address, singled out for particular attention "people taken hostage or who have disappeared in mysterious circumstances".
He said that liberating captives would be "a gesture that will fill with joy those who are waiting for it, but will also give peace to they (the hostage-takers) themselves".
Rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) have released some captives from the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima but negotiators saw no sign of an end to the siege.

The MRTA, which has said it has no intention of giving up its demands for the freedom of about 400 jailed comrades in exchange for the hostages, has called on Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori to start negotiations.
